card.name: Comma ending an introductory 'For...' clause
card.fires_on: The comma that closes an opening condition or 'For ...' phrase in dosing and preparation instructions. The next words are usually a directive such as 'see Table 1' or 'refer to'.

modes.label: For-phrase then cross-reference
modes.description: Comma after 'For dosage modifications/instructions for X' where the main clause points to another section or label.
modes.example: For dosing modifications for cisplatin, carboplatin, or pembrolizumab<<,>> refer to their prescribing information.

modes.label: If-condition then action
modes.description: Comma after an if-clause or a patient-condition phrase, leading to an instruction.
modes.example: If SYMVESS is accidentally nicked or cut during removal from the packaging bag<<,>> discard the damaged SYMVESS,

card.writes: It pushes the model to continue with directive verbs like refer, proceed, or treat.
card.plain: It marks the comma after a 'For this situation,' opener, just before the text tells you to see another section or take an action.
